title: Pregnancy care and the danger signs that mean go now

say: Pregnancy care, and the danger signs that mean go now.
This is the video for module 1 of Maternal and Child Health Literacy.
This module teaches one practical skill: knowing when a pregnant woman or new mother needs a health worker.

say: WHO, the World Health Organization, estimates that over 700 women die every day from causes linked to pregnancy and childbirth. WHO says most are preventable.

panel.heading: Most maternal deaths are preventable
items: First week: riskiest time for a newborn

say: Five complications cause about 75% of maternal deaths.

panel.heading: Most maternal deaths are preventable
items: First week: riskiest time for a newborn

say: The biggest is severe bleeding, mostly after the baby is born.

panel.heading: Most maternal deaths are preventable
items: First week: riskiest time for a newborn

say: Others are infections, high blood pressure, problems during delivery, and unsafe abortion.

panel.heading: Most maternal deaths are preventable
items: First week: riskiest time for a newborn

say: For newborns, about 75% of deaths happen in the first week of life.

say: When a woman dies from something treatable, time was usually lost. First, deciding at home. For example, Ngozi is 34 weeks pregnant with a severe headache and blurry eyes. Her sister says sleep, and she waits for her husband's permission.

panel.heading: Three delays, and how to cut them

cards.d: Nobody knows the sign, or the family waits for permission. Knowing the signs cuts this delay.
No car at night, no fare. A written plan for transport and money cuts this delay.
No records, so staff start from zero. Carry the antenatal card every time.

say: Second, getting there. At 10 pm the usual driver does not answer.

Each delay was avoidable: know the sign, agree in advance she can go, save a second driver's number, and keep the card in her bag.

say: Antenatal care is the care a woman gets from a skilled health worker during pregnancy. WHO recommends at least eight contacts.
The first should be in the first 12 weeks, so the early scan can be planned and iron and folic acid start early.

panel.heading: WHO: at least eight contacts
items: First contact in the first 12 weeks

say: Then at 20 and 26 weeks.

panel.heading: WHO: at least eight contacts
items: First contact in the first 12 weeks

say: Then 30 and 34 weeks.

panel.heading: WHO: at least eight contacts
items: First contact in the first 12 weeks

say: Then every two weeks in the last month, at 36, 38 and 40 weeks. Put the dates in your phone. If the clinic gives a different date, follow the clinic.

panel.heading: WHO: at least eight contacts
items: First contact in the first 12 weeks

say: And if you miss a visit, go as soon as you can. Do not feel ashamed to return.

panel.heading: WHO: at least eight contacts
items: First contact in the first 12 weeks
panel.rule: Missed a visit? Go as soon as you can. Late is better than never.

say: At each contact your blood pressure is checked, and you may get iron and folic acid, a scan, a tetanus vaccine and malaria prevention. The health worker decides the product and amount.
Take your card and ask what your results mean.

say: Each of these danger signs means go to a health facility now. Heavy bleeding, at any time. A severe headache that does not go away, or blurred vision, after 20 weeks. Pain high in the belly.
Fever or feeling very unwell, especially after birth. And any fit, which is an emergency.
Headache, blurred vision and upper belly pain can warn of pre-eclampsia, dangerously high blood pressure. If unsure, treat it as danger and go.

panel.heading: Danger signs in pregnancy and after birth

say: For example, Amaka is 30 weeks pregnant. She has had a bad headache all day and blurry eyes, and asks her neighbour Blessing if she should just lie down.
Blessing does not suggest any medicine. She says: these are danger signs, you need your blood pressure checked tonight.

panel.heading: Danger sign means go now
items: Do not wait to see if it gets better
No herbs or medicines on the way
Choose a facility that handles emergencies
Call the facility on the way

say: Choose a facility that can manage emergencies, such as a general hospital. Ask at antenatal care which hospital your clinic sends emergencies to.

say: Bring the card, and call ahead if you can. Blessing did not diagnose or treat. She removed the delay at home.

say: If a woman is having a fit, keep her away from fire, water and sharp objects.

panel.heading: If a woman is having a fit

cards.d: Keep her away from fire, water and sharp objects.
Lie her on her side once the fit allows. Do not put anything in her mouth.
Get her to a facility immediately. Eclampsia needs treatment only a facility can give.

say: And get her to a facility immediately.
After birth, watch the new mother's mind too. If she cannot cope or speaks about harming herself or the baby, she needs a health worker quickly. This is a health problem, not a weakness.

say: Say it simply to your family: bleeding, bad headache, blurred eyes, high belly pain, fever, fits. Go now, day or night, with the card.
And remember, this video supports a health worker. It never replaces one.
